mathgap.title: Direct count assignment
mathgap.principle: When a statement explicitly gives a numeric count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X has N items" appears.
mathgap.example: Treating "X has 5 oranges" as a relationship rather than assigning X = 5.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer than Y" as X = Y - N, preserving the order of the names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement contains the phrases "more than" or "fewer than".
mathgap.example: Reversing the order and writing Y = X + N instead of X = Y + N.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives N items to Y", subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count, using the counts after all earlier statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says that one person gives a specific number of items to another.
mathgap.example: Updating X and Y in the wrong order, or forgetting that earlier transfers may have changed X's count.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the exact order they appear; later statements must use the counts after all earlier updates have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For every problem, before using a statement, ensure all previous statements have been applied to the current state.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a later statement that should have used the updated count after a prior transfer.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a conditional transfer, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; if the condition holds, perform the transfer of all items from the giver to the receiver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y".
mathgap.example: Skipping the condition check and always performing the transfer, or transferring only N items instead of all of X's items.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Identify which equations and variables directly or indirectly affect the queried person, and ignore statements that cannot influence the target variable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, trace dependencies from the target variable through all equations and transfers.
mathgap.example: Spending time solving a large subsystem that has no path to the queried person.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality parsing
mathgap.principle: Parse statements of the form "The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have" as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a difference equality using the phrasing "more than" and "difference between".
mathgap.example: Swapping the order of terms and interpreting the equality as |A‑B| = |C‑D|, losing the sign information.

mathgap.title: Solve signed difference equations with unknowns
mathgap.principle: When a signed‑difference equality (A − B) = (C − D) contains unknown variables, rearrange it into a linear equation and solve for the unknowns using any known values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing a signed‑difference equality that still contains variables.
mathgap.example: Leaving the equation unsolved or treating it as two separate equations A‑B = 0 and C‑D = 0.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of X that Y has increases by p/q times" (or "by N times"), treat it as a multiplicative increase: new count = old count × (1 + p/q) (or old × (1 + N)). This yields an integer because the problem guarantees it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement contains the phrase "increases by … times" with a fraction or integer factor.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increase by 5/3 times" as adding 5/3 or multiplying by 5/3, instead of multiplying by 8/3.

mathgap.title: Equal redistribution and splitting handling
mathgap.principle: For "A and B redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount", set both A and B to (A + B) / 2. For "A splits all their items equally among B and C", set A to 0 and add half of A's original count to B and to C each. All operations use integer arithmetic as guaranteed by the problem.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement contains "redistribute ... to ensure each has an equal amount" or "splits all ... equally among ...".
mathgap.example: Treating "A splits all items equally among B and C" as giving each half while leaving A unchanged, instead of zeroing A and distributing half to each recipient.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misparses the phrasing of difference statements, losing the sign or reversing the order of the named variables.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Parse signed‑difference statements exactly as (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of names on each side and keeping the sign.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model updates counts without respecting the chronological order, using stale values for later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply every statement in the order presented, updating the state after each operation before processing the next.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as immutable, forgetting that later transfers can change that person's count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as initial values; always allow later statements (especially transfers) to modify them.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model skips the evaluation of the condition and either never performs the transfer or always performs it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if it holds, execute the transfer of all items.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting multiplicative increase statements as additive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the factor instead of multiplying, or multiplies by the factor alone, leading to incorrect counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply the rule: new = old × (1 + factor) for "increase by … times" statements.
